fact: The Justice Minister announced on 29 June 2026 that all 39 common-law first-instance courts are connected to the e-Justice platform, completing the first national phase, which began in January 2025 with two pilot courts.
TechAfrica News reports that sixteen more courts joined the national e-justice platform on 20 April 2026, bringing connected jurisdictions to 28, with further services to be added progressively.

Fraternité Matin reports that sixteen more courts were connected to the e-Justice.ci platform on 20 April 2026, bringing the network to 28 jurisdictions, with full national coverage as the stated goal.

The Justice Minister said the e-justice.ci platform became operational at the Abidjan-Plateau court of first instance on 26 June 2025, after pilots in Dabou and Yopougon in January 2025, and that all judicial procedures will be digitalised in the short term.

We Are Tech Africa reports Cote d'Ivoire launched its e-Justice platform in late January 2025, live for citizens in Yopougon and Dabou, to be extended to other jurisdictions and to harmonize the entire judicial system.
